newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: UBS acquires 11 pct in Hong Kong jeweler.
newsitem.headline: UBS acquires 11 pct in Hong Kong jeweler.

text.p: UBS Investment Management Ptd Ltd, the private equity arm of the Union Bank of Switzerland for the Far East, has acquired an 11 percent stake in Tse Sui Luen Jewellery (International) Ltd (TSL), a UBS statement said on Wednesday.
Listed on the Hong Kong stock exchange, TSL designs makes and sell jewelery in Hong Kong, China, Malaysia and Singapore.
David Lai, executive director at UBS Investment, told Reuters the acquisiton was a "strategic" one, but declined to reveal the price UBS paid.
UBS Investment manages funds of about US$300 million of which about 80 percent is the bank's own money.
Lai said UBS Investment usually buys into non-listed companies and this was the first time it bought a stake in a listed company.
He said TSL has many characteristics similar to unlisted firms which attract UBS, such as "being undervalued".
"The company has a good story in the China market...But it is undervalued, under researched and liquidity is low," he said.
Lai said he saw good "growth potential" for the group which reported a 31 percent rise in net profit last year.
"We expect it to maintain double digit growth. We like the China story and we have talked to management and they are making good margins and returns there."
Lai also said TSL was a major buyer of gold and UBS is the largest gold trader in Europe, though it does not currently sell to TSL.
There are plans for TSL to expand both in Europe and the United States and UBS should be able to help the company to penetrate these markets, he said.
